content.text: The ItemProcessor interface in Spring Batch allows you to process data between reading and writing in a batch job. It is an optional component in a chunk-oriented step but is commonly used for transformations, validations, or filtering.

items: I → Input type (type read by ItemReader)
O → Output type (type written by ItemWriter)
The process() method is called for each item read by the ItemReader.
Returning null in process() will filter out the item, so it is not passed to the writer.
This processor reads an Employee object and modifies its empName to uppercase.
Can also be used for data validation, filtering, or business logic transformation.
<Employee, Employee> → Input and output types are both Employee.
chunk(3) → Each transaction processes 3 records at a time.
This step reads from a database, transforms the employee names, and writes them to a JSON file.
The processor is seamlessly integrated into the chunk-oriented step.

rows: Convert text to uppercase, change date formats, calculate derived fields
Skip invalid records or throw exceptions for failed validations
Filter out records by returning null from process()
Add additional data from external services or APIs

items: ItemProcessor is optional, but recommended for separation of concerns.
Multiple processors can be chained using CompositeItemProcessor.
Processing happens between reading and writing in a chunk-oriented step.
Returning null → skips the item in writing phase.
